parsed_answer.content: Spring AOP (Aspect-Oriented Programming) solves the cross-cutting concern problem—where logic like logging, transaction management, or security is scattered across disparate business layers. Instead of polluting your service classes with boilerplate, AOP modularizes these concerns into Aspects. An Aspect is the unit of modularity that encapsulates the cross-cutting logic. The Pointcut acts as a predicate expression that determines exactly which JoinPoints—the specific execution moments in your application, such as method calls or exception handling—should trigger the associated Advice. Advice is the actual action taken at a specific JoinPoint, such as 'before' or 'after' the method execution. Finally, Weaving is the process of linking these aspects with the target objects. In Spring, this happens at runtime via dynamic proxies, creating a decorated object that intercepts calls to apply the advice.

items: Spring AOP uses JDK Dynamic Proxies if the target object implements interfaces, or CGLIB (Code Generation Library) to subclass the target class if no interfaces are present.
The proxy pattern intercepts method calls, checks if any Pointcuts match the method signature, and if so, invokes the Advice chain before delegating the call to the actual bean instance.

Weaving in Spring is 'Runtime Weaving', which means there is a slight performance overhead compared to AspectJ's compile-time weaving, but it provides seamless integration with the Spring IoC container.
The JoinPoint object provides reflective access to the method arguments, the target object, and the signature, allowing the Advice to inspect or modify the execution context.

parsed_answer.content: A classic production pitfall is the 'self-invocation' problem. Because Spring AOP uses proxies, if a method inside your bean calls another method within the same class (e.g., this.doWork()), the call bypasses the proxy entirely. The Advice will not trigger. Always move cross-cutting logic to a separate service or use AopContext.currentProxy() if you absolutely must trigger an aspect from within the same class.
